label: Updated at 8 p.m. ET
title: Today In Golf
summary: A 30-second briefing on today's biggest golf stories.

items.headline: DeChambeau’s Open Penalty Costs
items.text: Bryson DeChambeau said a two-stroke penalty and a triple-bogey at The Open cost him a chance at the Claret Jug; he finished T14 at 4-under while Ryan Fox led at 10-under.

items.headline: NZ Could Host Presidents Cup
items.text: Ryan Fox suggested New Zealand isn’t likely to host a full-time PGA Tour event but could host a one-off Presidents Cup, supported by Scottie Scheffler’s recent comments.

items.headline: DeChambeau’s Near-Miss on Poulter
items.text: Ian Poulter nearly got hit in the ear by a tee shot from Bryson DeChambeau at LIV Golf UK, caused by a blind landing area from a new tee box configuration.
